    action=time.set

    impl=read
    semantics=action
    action=time.read
    doc="A sentence about the calendar or the clock read whole by the world's reader: a day, month or season n steps after or before another or today (the library's cycleAdd), the days between two days (cycleDiff), the season of a month, the months of a season, the weekend, the days of a month, units of time in units of time (k.time durations), the time n hours or minutes after or before a time, the hours between two times (readClock, writeClock)."

# time.calendar: the calendar and the clock (kids plan, ADR-011; Q18 K7, L2). The patterns above the GENERATED marker hand the sentence to the world's own reader (ops.mjs
# `readTime`): a sentence that names a day, a month, a season, a unit of time, today / tomorrow / yesterday or the clock is read whole with the names and durations of
# k.time, the words of lang.common's lang.time.* and the numbers, prepositions and question words of w.lang.en; the library's cycleAdd / cycleDiff / statedDay /
# readClock / writeClock do the arithmetic. A sentence the reader does not read whole is declined (`accepts`), so the next world reads it. No phrasing is listed here.

    namespace=time.calendar
    version=0.1.0
    legend=$legend.time.calendar
    imports=world.core
    imports=world.lang.common
    imports=world.acts
    replaces=world.kids.time
    formalization=rules
    reader=yes
    language=en
    status=fixture
    title="The calendar and the clock"
    summary="count days, months, seasons and hours"
    doc="A general world, not a tab (kids plan, ADR-011; Q18 K7, L2): the days of the week, the months and the seasons as cycles of k.time, the days of a month, units of time in units of time, and the 12-hour clock. Statements and questions of today, the month, the season and the time are the catalog's frames (w.lang.en time-frames, generated by scripts/build-time-world.mjs with the lexicons the catalog derives from k.time); every other sentence that names a day, a month, a season, a unit of time or the clock is read whole by the world's own reader (ops.mjs readTime) and the library does the arithmetic (cycleAdd, cycleDiff, statedDay, readClock, writeClock). Today and the time are the host's (the device clock) until the dialogue states them. Hand-built platform fixture, not produced by the C1 workflow."
